**Notice, what follows is generated by AI.**

To quickly learn and start using KaTeX in your project, follow these steps:

1. **Include KaTeX in your project:**
   - Via CDN: Add the following lines to the `<head>` section of your HTML file:
     ```html
     <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.1/dist/katex.min.css" integrity="sha384-Xi8rHCmBmhbuyyKjQm7Np5NkeutA0AAAyr0aeHblUBg+uoebFJK5DA0eM0Ry4cZl9Q" crossorigin="anonymous">
     <script defer src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.1/dist/katex.min.js" integrity="sha384-3q1uQJN1GZl2eYzV7WtLq0fJQmQXyG4KJbYwTqX2Kx2b0k3yPPb7tT6Brh0V0dDyJ0" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
     ```
   - Or, if you prefer, download KaTeX and include the necessary CSS and JavaScript files from your local directory.

2. **Set up the auto-rendering feature (optional):**
   To automatically render all LaTeX math in your document, include the auto-render extension:
   ```html
   <script defer src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.1/dist/contrib/auto-render.min.js" integrity="sha384-vZTG03m+2yp6N6BNi5iM4rW4oIwk5DfcNdFgyJQQ6iQfQGjwfgXyFcfphbKZsYn" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
   <script>
     document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function() {
       renderMathInElement(document.body, {
         delimiters: [
           {left: "$$", right: "$$", display: true},
           {left: "\\(", right: "\\)", display: false},
           // Add more delimiters if needed
         ]
       });
     });
   </script>
   ```

3. **Write LaTeX code:**
   Surround your LaTeX math expressions with the appropriate delimiters. For inline math, use `\( ... \)`, and for display math, use `$$ ... $$` or `\[ ... \]`.

   Example:
   ```html
   <p>Inline math: \( \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5 \)</p>
   <p>Display math:</p>
   $$ \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-x^2} dx = \sqrt{\pi} $$
   // mayb need to delete the "<p>" and "</p>"
   ```
   Inline math: \( \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5 \)
   Display math:
   $$ \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-x^2} dx = \sqrt{\pi} $$

4. **Customize (if needed):**
   KaTeX offers options for customization such as color, font size, and more. You can explore the documentation for advanced usage and styling.

5. **Practice and refer to resources:**
   - Visit the official KaTeX website (<https://katex.org/>) for documentation, examples, and a live demo.
   - Use online LaTeX editors or tutorials to practice writing LaTeX syntax if you're not familiar with it yet.
   - Experiment with different expressions in your own project to see how they render.

By following these steps, you should be able to integrate KaTeX into your project and start rendering mathematical expressions quite quickly. Practice with various LaTeX expressions to get comfortable with the syntax and KaTeX's capabilities.
